lines.text: F. 272. Περὶ τῆς μεθόδου τῶν Χαρανιτῶν 1 ἤτοι ἐναλλαγῆς
lines.en: F. 272. On the method of the Charanians 1 or the change

lines.text: Ἰδὲ κατὰ τὰς ιθʹ τοῦ Ἰουλίου μηνὸς νυκτί, [τῆς] ἐπιφωσκούσης
lines.en: Look on the night of the 19th of the month of July, as it dawns

lines.text: τῆς κʹ τοῦ αὐτοῦ μηνός 2, καὶ ἔνθα ἄν ἐστιν ἡ Σελήνη, ἐκεῖνο τὸ ζῴδιον
lines.en: on the 20th of the same month 2, and wherever the Moon is, that zodiac sign

lines.text: λόγισαι ὡροσκόπον τοῦ κοσμικοῦ ἔτους, καὶ εἰ εὕρῃς τὴν Σελήνην ἐν
lines.en: reckon as the ascendant of the cosmic year, and if you find the Moon in

lines.text: τῷ Κριῷ, πολλαὶ συννέφειαι καὶ ὑετοὶ ἔσονται <κατὰ> τὸ ἔτος ἐκεῖνο
lines.en: Aries, there will be many clouds and rains <during> that year

lines.text: καὶ ὁ σῖτος ἔσται λεπτὸς καὶ τὸ ἔλαιον πληθυνθήσεται. εἰ δὲ ἐν τῷ
lines.en: and the wheat will be thin and the oil will be multiplied. But if in

lines.text: Ταύρῳ, ἔσται ὑετὸς πολὺς κατὰ τὴν ἀρχὴν τοῦ ἔτους καὶ τὸ τέλος
lines.en: Taurus, there will be much rain at the beginning of the year and the end

lines.text: καὶ φόβος ἐν τῇ γῇ πολὺς καὶ ψῦχος πολὺ καὶ παγετὸς καὶ πόλεμοι
lines.en: and much fear on the earth and much cold and frost and wars

sections.en: I described codex B(ononiensis); Leo Parmentier collated for me codex A(ngelicanus) 29, 13th c., f. 14v. I have mostly not noted orthographical matters. 1 χειρανήτων B. ἐναλαγή B. 3 ἴδε codd. τὰς] read τὴν? 3-4 τῆς ἐπιφωσκούσεως codd. 5 λόγησε B. ἐν omitted by B. 6 συνεφίαι codd. τὸ ἔτος ἐκεῖνο (without κατὰ) B : τῷ χρόνῳ ἐκείνῳ A. 7 ὁ omitted by B. 7-8 ἡ δὲ ζῳδίω Ταύρου B. 8 τοῦ τέλους codd. : corrected. 9 ἐν omitted by B. 9-10 πολὴς B. πόλεων διαφορὰ B.

sections.text:
1 Charanitae sunt Sabaei Carrhenses qui temporibus cum Romanorum tum
Arabum astrologiae studiosi fuerunt; cf. Catal. Flor., p. 84, n. 5. De his Sabaeis
notus est liber viri doctissimi Chwolsohn, Die Ssabier, 1856. Ad cultum planetarum
spectant nova fragmenta a De Goeje et Dozy edita (Nouveaux documents pour
l'étude de la religion des Harraniens (Actes Congrès Orient. Leyde, 1885, 2e partie,
p. 281 ss.).
2 Die 19 vel 20 Iulii, quo Canicula exoritur (cf. Pseudo-Gemini calendarium ap.
Lydi, De Ost., ed. Wachsmuth, p. 151, 19 ss.), antiqui astrologi caelum servare
solebant “ coniecturamque capere salubrisne an pestilens annus futurus esset „;
cf. Heraclidem Ponticum ap. Ciceronem, De div., I, 57; Syrum in Catal. Flor.,
p. 171; Hephaest. Theb., I, 23 (p. 91, Engelbrecht). — Eadem fere atque Charanitae
docet Zoroaster in Geoponicis I, 8 (p. 17, 4 ss. ed. Beckh) sed non de duobus
solum, ut Apomasaris codices, sed de duodecim zodiaci signis agit. Vide etiam
quae ad excerptum Antiochi quod ex cod. Neap. 19, f. 433v infra edetur adnota-
vimus.
sections.en:
1 The Charanians are the Sabaeans of Carrhae who in the times of both the Romans and the Arabs were students of astrology; cf. Catal. Flor., p. 84, n. 5. Concerning these Sabaeans the book of the most learned man Chwolsohn, Die Ssabier, 1856, is well known. New fragments edited by De Goeje and Dozy pertain to the cult of the planets (Nouveaux documents pour l'étude de la religion des Harraniens (Actes Congrès Orient. Leyde, 1885, 2nd part, p. 281 ff.).
2 On the 19th or 20th of July, when the Dog Star rises (cf. the calendar of Pseudo-Geminus in Lydus, De Ost., ed. Wachsmuth, p. 151, 19 ff.), ancient astrologers were accustomed to observe the sky “and to make a conjecture whether the future year would be healthy or pestilential”; cf. Heraclides Ponticus in Cicero, De div., I, 57; Syrus in Catal. Flor., p. 171; Hephaestio of Thebes, I, 23 (p. 91, Engelbrecht). — Zoroaster teaches almost the same things as the Charanians in the Geoponica I, 8 (p. 17, 4 ff. ed. Beckh) but he treats not only of two, as the codices of Apomasar do, but of the twelve signs of the zodiac. See also what we have noted on the excerpt of Antiochus which will be edited below from cod. Neap. 19, f. 433v.

summary.headline: Apomasar on the Cosmic Year
summary.text: Excerpt from Apomasar on the Charanian method for predicting the cosmic year: the Moon’s zodiac sign at dawn on July 20 determines the ascendant, with Aries indicating clouds, rain, thin wheat, and abundant oil, and Taurus indicating rain, fear, cold, frost, wars, and famine.
